title: Registry records and routing contract (draft)
content:
Summary:
This note captures a pragmatic control-plane registry model and the corresponding HTTP CRUD contract that supports multi-region replication and routing policy lookup. The goal is to have a small, opinionated resource record and clear API semantics so downstream systems (router, rollout orchestrator, SRE) can build predictable behavior without complex cross-region coordination.

Key objects and identities (plain english):
- Resource record: canonical entity stored in the registry. Every record has an immutable UUID primary id and a stable human name that is unique within its parent scope.
- Kinds: environment, region, cluster, routing_policy, generic_resource. Kind determines expected attributes and validation.
- Parent scoping: many objects are scoped under a parent id; for example a cluster is scoped under a region which is scoped under an environment. Parent ids are recorded on the record.

Record fields (recommended minimal shape):
- id: uuid (immutable)
- name: short string (unique in parent)
- kind: one of the supported kinds
- parent_id: uuid or empty
- metadata: free-form string map encoded as JSON in the metadata field (store as a string blob at the HTTP level)
- version: integer, monotonic increment on each accepted mutation
- etag: opaque string used for If-Match/If-None-Match conditional requests
- deleted: literal string "true" or "false" for tombstone semantics

Notes on encoding: store metadata as a JSON-encoded string so the top-level resource record remains a flat key map for our storage and indexers. Validation enforces size limits on the metadata blob.

CRUD API contract (HTTP endpoints and high-level behavior):
- Create: POST /v1/records
  - request may include a client-supplied id; server will accept it if it is a valid UUID and the create is idempotent.
  - server sets version=1 and returns Location header with the record id plus an etag header.
- Read: GET /v1/records/{id}
  - returns the latest live record; includes ETag and X-Resource-Version headers.
- Update: PATCH /v1/records/{id}
  - optimistic concurrency via If-Match header with the current ETag.
  - partial updates merged into the existing record; server increments version and returns new ETag.
  - client operations may include an operation_id header for idempotent retry.
- Replace: PUT /v1/records/{id}
  - full replace semantics; still requires If-Match for safety on non-blank replaces.
- Delete: DELETE /v1/records/{id}
  - soft delete: record.deleted becomes "true", version increments, and a tombstone event is emitted.
- List / filter: GET /v1/records?kind=cluster&parent_id=<uuid>&label=gpu:a100
  - supports paging; list includes tombstone flag so callers can filter out deleted records.

Concurrency and safety patterns:
- Use If-Match with etag for updates. 412 returned on mismatch.
- Do not rely on distributed transactions. Instead, publish every accepted change as an event to a change-log (CDC stream). Replicas subscribe and apply events in order.
- Event tuple includes: record id, new version, origin region, actor id, request id, and an opaque payload (the record snapshot or delta).
- For deterministic conflict resolution under concurrent cross-region writes, use the (version, origin_timestamp, origin_region_id) ordering where the higher version wins, and origin_region_id is a deterministic tie-breaker.

Multi-region replication and GC:
- Active-active writes are allowed; replication is asynchronous. The CDC stream is the source of truth for replica updates.
- Tombstones persist for a configurable retention window (default 30 days) before final GC. Final GC is coordinated by a single region leader to avoid race conditions.

Routing policy primitives:
- A routing policy is a registry record with kind=routing_policy. It contains selectors, a numeric priority, and an optional fallback policy id.
- Selectors are expressed as a flat list of selector strings. Examples of selector strings: "id:cluster-uuid-...", "label:gpu=a100", "region:eu-west-2". Keep the selector DSL intentionally small.
- Evaluation: router loads routing policies (cache TTL ~1s) and evaluates selectors against the cluster inventory which is maintained by the control-plane. If no selector matches, router consults the fallback policy id if present.

Operational guidelines for the router integration:
- Cache policy: Router must tolerate slightly stale policies; use a short TTL and fall back to last-known-good when control-plane is unreachable.
- Emit observability tags when routing decisions are made: policy_id, cluster_id, environment, and region.
- Health filtering: Router must consult cluster health and capacity metadata before selecting a target cluster; control-plane provides health metadata in the records.

Audit and event model:
- Every accepted mutation is published to the change-log with actor and request id for trace. The log entry is the primary replication artifact.
- Include human-readable audit text in the event for operator debugging.

Open design questions and proposals for follow-up:
- How to support bulk onboarding: propose an async bulk import endpoint that returns a job id and per-item failure reasons; the job emits events for each successful import.
- Rename collisions across regions: propose to allow origin-region to enforce name uniqueness and to append audit suffixes on conflict during replication reconciliation.
- Schema evolution: add typed fields only after a migration window; keep metadata blob for additive fields until migration completes.

Action items (owners):
- Draft ETag format and write examples (owner: Priya Nair).
- Prototype minimal CDC event envelope and simple replication harness (owner: Omar Farouk).
- Draft RBAC mapping for record-level operations and map to IAM roles (owner: Lena Cho).

Appendix: quick examples (textual):
- Create cluster example (text only): POST /v1/records with fields: kind=cluster, name=eu-west-2-gpu, parent_id=<region-uuid>, metadata=<json-string-of-labels>. Server responds with 201, Location pointing to the new id, and ETag header.
- Partial update example: PATCH /v1/records/<cluster-id> with If-Match set to the latest ETag and metadata updated. Successful update returns 200 with new ETag and X-Resource-Version.

This draft is intentionally compact. Once we converge, convert to a Confluence spec that includes sequence diagrams for replication and routing evaluation flows.
